question.prompt: The hypotenuse of a right triangle is \(10\) inches and the radius of the inscribed circle is \(1\) inch. The perimeter of the triangle in inches is:

solutions.explanation:
Equal tangent lengths let us compare the sum of the legs directly with the hypotenuse. Name the triangle \(ABC\), with right angle at \(C\) and \(AB=10\). Let the incircle have center \(I\), touching \(CA,CB,AB\) at \(D,E,F\), respectively.

A radius to a tangent is perpendicular to that tangent. Hence \(CDIE\) has four right angles. Its adjacent sides \(ID\) and \(IE\) are both radii of length \(1\), so it is a square. Therefore \(CD=CE=1\).

Set \(AF=u\) and \(BF=v\). Then \(u+v=AB=10\). Tangent segments from the same exterior point have equal lengths, giving \(AD=AF=u\) and \(BE=BF=v\). Thus
\[
AC=u+1,\qquad BC=v+1.
\]
The perimeter is
\[
AB+AC+BC
=10+(u+v)+2=22.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{22\text{ inches}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Use equal tangent lengths

solutions.explanation:
The area connects the inradius to the perimeter, so we can find the sum of the legs without finding either leg separately. Let the positive leg lengths be \(a\) and \(b\), and let \(I\) be the incenter.

The right triangle has area \(ab/2\). Joining \(I\) to the three vertices splits it into three triangles. Their bases are the three sides, and each height is the inradius \(1\). Consequently,
\[
\frac{ab}{2}=\frac{a+b+10}{2},
\qquad ab=a+b+10.
\]
The Pythagorean theorem gives \(a^2+b^2=100\). Combining these relations,
\[
\begin{aligned}
(a+b-10)(a+b+10)
&=(a+b)^2-100\\
&=2ab\\
&=2(a+b+10).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(a+b+10>0\), dividing by this factor is valid and gives \(a+b-10=2\). Thus \(a+b=12\), and the perimeter is \(12+10=\boxed{22\text{ inches}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Compare two area expressions
